frameworks.scope: All entities required to apply IFRS Accounting Standards
frameworks.effectiveDate: Annual periods beginning on or after 1 Jan 2024
frameworks.digitalTaxonomy: IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Taxonomy (XBRL) — draft Feb 2024, final Q4 2024

aiRecommendation.reasoning: ISSB S1/S2 effective for FY 2024. Scope 3 with 1-year deferral — first Scope 3 disclosure due FY 2025. Adopting XBRL taxonomy once finalised. Aligned with TCFD recommendations.

frameworks.jurisdiction: EU (large companies + non-EU companies with EUR 150M+ EU turnover)
frameworks.scope: Large EU companies (250+ employees, EUR 50M turnover) + listed SMEs + non-EU companies (CSRD wave 3, 2028)
frameworks.assuranceLevel: limited (from 2028); reasonable (Commission decision, no earlier than 2028)
frameworks.effectiveDate: FY 2024 (NFRD companies); FY 2025 (other large EU); FY 2026 (listed SMEs); FY 2028 (non-EU wave 3)
frameworks.digitalTaxonomy: ESRS XBRL Taxonomy (EFRAG, Aug 2024) — mandatory from 2028
frameworks.scenarioApproach: IEA scenarios including NZE, STEPS, AP

aiRecommendation.action: ESRS is most demanding — use as long-form, extract ISSB+SEC via crosswalk
aiRecommendation.reasoning: Double materiality basis captures most info. No Scope 3 deferral. Limited assurance from 2028. Recommend preparing ESRS-compliant report as primary, with ISSB and SEC disclosures extracted via mapping crosswalk.

frameworks.jurisdiction: US (SEC registrants — domestic + foreign private issuers)
frameworks.scope: All SEC registrants (phased by filer status: LAF, AF, SRC, EGC)
frameworks.scope3Deferral: n/a — only required if entity has Scope 3 target (10% safe harbour for 3 years)
frameworks.digitalTaxonomy: inline XBRL for Scope 1+2 (from FY 2026) — no climate-specific taxonomy yet

aiRecommendation.action: Continue SEC Climate Rule compliance — extract from ESRS long-form
aiRecommendation.reasoning: SEC Climate Rule in effect for LAF from FY 2024. Scope 1+2 with assurance from FY 2029. Scope 3 only if target set (we have not set Scope 3 target — not required). Single-scenario approach less demanding than ESRS/ISSB. Extract from ESRS report via crosswalk.

climateScenarios.keyCharacteristics: Early, gradual policy tightening; transition costs offset by avoided damages
climateScenarios.supervisoryUse: Used as 'policy ambition' benchmark by ECB and Bank of England

aiRecommendation.action: Continue using Orderly as ambition benchmark
aiRecommendation.reasoning: Orderly scenario projects USD 185M portfolio impact (mostly transition risk in fossil fuel exposures). Used as ECB climate stress test ambition benchmark. Recommend continuing as primary 'transition ambition' scenario.

climateScenarios.keyCharacteristics: Late policy tightening; abrupt carbon price spike; stranded assets
climateScenarios.supervisoryUse: Adverse scenario for short-term stress testing (e.g. Bank of England CBES 2022)

aiRecommendation.action: Use as adverse scenario for short-term stress testing
aiRecommendation.reasoning: Disorderly scenario projects USD 412M portfolio impact, driven by stranded fossil fuel assets in oil & gas sector. Carbon price spike USD 30→300 between 2030-2040. Recommend as primary 'transition shock' adverse scenario.

climateScenarios.keyCharacteristics: No policy tightening; severe physical risk; sea level rise, extreme heat, crop failure
climateScenarios.supervisoryUse: Physical risk resilience testing; real estate & agriculture exposure stress

aiRecommendation.action: Use as physical risk adverse scenario — review real estate exposure
aiRecommendation.reasoning: Hot House scenario projects USD 678M portfolio impact, dominated by physical risk in real estate (Miami, Houston coastal properties) and agricultural loans (California Central Valley). 3C warming with regional 4-5C variation. Recommend immediate review of physical risk exposure concentrations.

climateScenarios.keyCharacteristics: Rapid coordinated transition; 45% emissions cut by 2030 vs 2010; net zero by 2050
climateScenarios.supervisoryUse: Ambition benchmark for ISSB S2 1.5C-aligned scenario requirement

aiRecommendation.action: Continue using Net Zero as ISSB S2 1.5C-aligned scenario
aiRecommendation.reasoning: Net Zero 2050 projects USD 98M portfolio impact (lowest of any scenario). Satisfies ISSB S2 requirement for at least one 1.5C-aligned scenario. Carbon price reaches USD 700/tonne by 2050. Recommend as primary 'Paris-aligned ambition' scenario.

socialMetrics.metricName: Critical-tier models with bias testing completed

aiRecommendation.reasoning: All 4 Critical-tier models completed bias testing in reporting period. DIR results: 0.87, 0.91, 0.84, 0.78. One model (MODEL-INS-UNDER-004) below 0.80 EEOC threshold — under mandatory remediation.

MODEL-INS-UNDER-004 (Insurance Underwriting) DIR 0.78 — below 0.80 threshold. Mandatory remediation due within 90 days. Interim mitigation: manual review of all underwriting decisions for protected class applicants.

socialMetrics.metricName: Products subject to Consumer Duty outcome monitoring

aiRecommendation.action: Continue Consumer Duty monitoring across 47 products
aiRecommendation.reasoning: All 47 retail products subject to FCA Consumer Duty Outcome monitoring. Fair value assessments completed for all 47 in reporting period. 3 product modifications made following outcome monitoring.

aiRecommendation.action: Continue vulnerable customer identification + enhanced support
aiRecommendation.reasoning: 184,723 vulnerable customers identified (6.5% of customer base). Within FCA expected range (5-8%). Enhanced support arrangements in place: dedicated phone line, extended processing times, simplified communications.

aiRecommendation.reasoning: Board at 44% female (above 40% target). ExCo at 38% (below 40% target). Overall workforce 45% female. Gender pay gap 7.2% (median), down from 8.4% prior year.

socialMetrics.quantitativeThreshold: Disclosure of % at each seniority band

aiRecommendation.action: Continue trajectory toward ExCo ethnic minority representation target
aiRecommendation.reasoning: Board at 22% ethnic minority (above Parker Review 20% target for FTSE 350). ExCo at 17% (below 20% target). Pay equity audit completed; 12 pay adjustments made.

aiRecommendation.action: Continue community investment at current trajectory
aiRecommendation.reasoning: USD 18.5M total community investment in reporting period. Financial inclusion is largest category (USD 7.2M) — supports 14 basic bank account products and 8 microfinance partnerships. 1,247 bank branches in low-income/underserved areas.

socialMetrics.metricName: Bank branches in low-income / underserved areas

aiRecommendation.action: INVESTIGATE — branch closures in underserved areas exceeding replacement rate
aiRecommendation.reasoning: 11 net branch closures in low-income/underserved areas year-on-year. Replacement rate via digital banking services at 78% (below 90% target). 'Banking desert' risk identified in 3 rural census tracts. Recommend review of branch closure methodology.
